<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**[[Mya Thwe Thwe Khaing]], a young protester who was shot in the head last week, dies from her injuries, the first death since the opposition to the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] began and as pressure on the [[Tatmadaw|military]] mounts. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/myanmar-protester-dies-after-10-days-on-life-support-pressure-on-army-grows-idUSKBN2AJ02E?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**Two [[Law enforcement in India|policemen]] are killed by unidentified gunmen at close range in [[Srinagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/jk-militants-open-fire-police-shot-dead-srinagar-7195637/ (The Indian Express)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Megxit]]
**[[Buckingham Palace]] announces that [[Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex]] and [[Meghan, Duchess of Sussex]] will be stripped of their royal patronages and honorary military appointments following a review of the royal couple's position within the [[British royal family]]. The couple will retain their [[Royal Highness|HRH]] titles but will no longer use them. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/feb/19/harry-meghan-tell-queen-not-return-working-royals (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*''[[Uber BV v Aslam]]''
**The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|UK Supreme Court]], in a unanimous decision, orders [[Uber]] to classify its drivers as employees, entitling them to minimum wage and paid leave. [https://www.wired.co.uk/article/uber-loses-gig-economy-case (''Wired'')]
*[[Bitcoin]] reaches a [[United States dollar|US$]]1 trillion [[Market capitalization|market cap]] for the first time. [https://www.reuters.com/article/crypto-currency-bitcoin-int/bitcoin-hits-1-trillion-market-cap-soars-to-another-record-high-idUSKBN2AJ19W (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****[[Ministry of Health (Czech Republic)|Health Minister]] Jan Blatný announces that shops will not be allowed to reopen on February 22, unlike what was previously promised. He also announced that residents will be required to wear [[FFP2]] respirators, nanotowels, or two [[surgical mask]]s in indoor places and on public transport due to the spread of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]]. [https://brnodaily.com/2021/02/19/news/politics/respirators-required-from-monday-but-shops-stay-closed/ (BRNO Daily)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports its first three cases of the Lineage P.1 variant in people who travelled from [[Brazil]]. [https://amp.rte.ie/amp/1198206/ (RTÉ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****[[Senate (Netherlands)|Senator]]s vote 45–13 to approve legislation that underpins the curfew, ensuring that it will continue until March despite an initial court order to end it. [https://apnews.com/article/netherlands-bills-legislation-coronavirus-pandemic-the-hague-6945991a0703e685727fdaa3e710fe74 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Poland]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://tvn24.pl/polska/koronawirus-w-polsce-pierwszy-przypadek-mutacji-poludniowoafrykanskiej-5024421 (TVN24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] receives one million doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], a day after it was approved for emergency use in the city. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/health-environment/article/3122338/coronavirus-hong-kong-official-defends-safety (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] detects a new [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] from 91 cases in the [[Kanto region]] and two cases at airports. In addition, an infection cluster is detected at a [[Tokyo]] [[immigration to Japan|immigration]] facility. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-19/japan-finds-90-cases-of-new-covid-19-strain-media-reports/13172142 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports 157 deaths in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total in five months, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 11,829. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/02/19/21/ph-logs-1901-new-covid-19-cases-reported-deaths-highest-in-over-5-months (ABS-CBN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zambia]]
****[[Zambia]] surpasses 1,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/africa/2021-02/19/c_139753081.htm (Xinhua)]
***[[Africa]] surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://apnews.com/article/africa-100k-coronavirus-deaths-2afd198dccff5f62f0eaa01da501956e (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Florida]] reports their first case of the Brazil variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]], making it the fourth state to do so after [[Minnesota]], [[Oklahoma]], and [[Maryland]]. [https://www.abcactionnews.com/news/state/cdc-first-case-of-brazil-p-1-coronavirus-variant-reported-in-florida (WFTS-TV)]
****[[Florida]] surpasses 30,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/coronavirus/article249372025.html (''Miami Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Idaho]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Idaho]] reports their first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from [[Southwestern Idaho]] who previously travelled internationally. [https://www.idahostatesman.com/news/coronavirus/article249371890.html (''Idaho Statesman'')]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Johnson & Johnson]] submits an application of its experimental single-dose [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to the [[World Health Organization]] for emergency authorization. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/jj-submits-application-for-its-covid-19-vaccine-to-the-who-2021-02-19 (Marketwatch)] 
*[[2020–21 H5N8 outbreak]]
**[[Hong Kong]] suspends the import of [[poultry]] meat and products from [[bird flu]]-affected areas in [[South Korea]], [[Germany]] and [[Poland]] due to spread of highly pathogenic [[H5N8]] in those areas. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/hong-kong-suspends-import-of-poultry-products-from-bird-flu-affected-areas (''The Straits Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[47th G7 summit]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] and [[Prime Minister of Italy|Italian Prime Minister]] [[Mario Draghi]] make their first global appearance at a virtual [[Group of Seven|G7]] meeting as the countries discuss COVID-19 recovery, trade, social media, free speech, and their approach to [[China]]. The countries also commit to offer $7.5 billion in funding for vaccination rollouts in poor countries. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210219-g7-leaders-commit-7-5-billion-to-vaccine-rollout-in-poor-countries (France 24)]
**President Biden, in a reversal of the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s approach to the COVID-19 pandemic, says that the [[United States]] will contribute up to $4 billion to [[COVAX]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/biden-covid-vaccine-covax-4-billion-pledge-poor-countries-coronavirus-equity/ (CBS News)]
*[[Environmental policy of the Joe Biden administration]]
**The [[United States]] formally rejoins the [[Paris Agreement]], 107 days after it [[United States withdrawal from the Paris Agreement|left the climate accord]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/feb/19/us-official-return-paris-climate-pact (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Equatorial Guinea–Israel relations]]
**[[President of Equatorial Guinea|Equatoguinean President]] [[Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo]] announces that his country will move its [[embassy]] from [[Tel Aviv]] to [[Jerusalem]] following talks with [[Israel]]i [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/equatorial-guinea-to-move-embassy-to-jerusalem-israel/2150717 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''Law and crime'''
*In a 6–1 decision, the [[Federal Court of Malaysia]] rules that news portal ''[[Malaysiakini]]'' can be held in [[contempt of court]] over its users' comments against the [[Judiciary of Malaysia|Malaysian judiciary]]. Co-founder and [[editor-in-chief]] [[Steven Gan]] is personally absolved of the [[criminal charge|charge]]. The portal will be required to pay [[Malaysian ringgit|RM]]500,000 (about [[United States dollar|US$]]120,000) in fines next week. [https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/563554 (''Malaysiakini'')] [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysiakini-found-contempt-of-court-readers-comments-steven-gan-14233454 (CNA)]
*A [[Sudan]]ese [[asylum seeker]] stabs an immigration official to death at a refugee centre in [[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]], [[France]]. The attack is not thought to be linked to [[Terrorism in France|terrorism]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-56130417 (BBC News)]
*[[National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine|Ukrainian National Security and Defense Council]] secretary [[Oleksiy Danilov]] announces sanctions on pro-Russian opposition leader [[Viktor Medvedchuk]] for allegedly using [[coal mine]]s in the [[Luhansk Oblast]] to finance [[Separatist forces of the war in Donbass|separatists]]. The government also announced that it would [[Nationalization|nationalize]] a pipeline that transports Russian oil into the rest of [[Europe]], which Medvedchuk was suspected of owning. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ukraine-sanctions/ukraine-sanctions-kremlin-ally-medvedchuk-says-will-take-back-fuel-pipeline-idUSKBN2AJ28O?il=0 (Reuters)] 
*The [[Brazil|Brazilian]] [[Chamber of Deputies (Brazil)|Chamber of Deputies]] votes 364–130 to confirm the [[Supreme Federal Court]]-mandated arrest of congressman Daniel Silveira ([[Social Liberal Party (Brazil)|PSL]]-[[Rio de Janeiro (state)|RJ]]) for posting videos online threatening the judges of the Court, calling for the Court's extinction and for a new [[Institutional Act Number Five|AI-5]] – considered the most repressive legal instrument of the former [[Military dictatorship in Brazil|Brazilian military government]]. His party is also considering his expulsion. [https://www.en24news.com/e/2021/02/a-brazilian-deputy-arrested-for-insulting-supreme-court-justices-in-a-video.html (EN24)] [https://g1.globo.com/politica/noticia/2021/02/19/camara-decide-manter-na-prisao-o-deputado-daniel-silveira.ghtml (''O Globo'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Turks and Caicos Islands general election]]
**The opposition [[Progressive National Party (Turks and Caicos Islands)|Progressive National Party]] wins 14 of the 15 seats in the [[House of Assembly (Turks and Caicos Islands)|House of Assembly]], with [[Washington Misick]] slated to become the next [[Premier of the Turks and Caicos Islands|premier]]. Outgoing Premier [[Sharlene Cartwright-Robinson]] of the [[People's Democratic Movement (Turks and Caicos Islands)|People's Democratic Movement]] loses re-election to her seat. [https://suntci.com/opposition-party-wins-landslide-election-in-turks-and-caicos-islands-p5848-129.htm (''Turks & Caicos Sun'')]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Argentina|Argentine]] [[Ministry of Health (Argentina)|Health Minister]] [[Ginés González García]] resigns amid scandal over preferential treatment for the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine]] to his close friends, including journalist [[Horacio Verbitsky]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/argentine-health-minister-resigns-amid-vaccine-scandal/2021/02/19/42d71a70-7305-11eb-8651-6d3091eac63f_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
